senses: writ of judgment or judgement, sentence
la:noun:periculum.html:
pĕrīcŭlum (contr. pĕrīclum, very freq. in the poets, e. g. ; ; ; ; ; et saep.; ; ; et saep.; ), i, n.
root, Sanscr. par, pi-par-mi, to conduct, guide; Gr. περάω, to pierce; πόρος. a way through, passage; Lat. porta, portus, ex - perior, per-itus; cf. Germ. fahren, Gefahr
,
a trial, experiment, attempt, proof, essay (class.; cf. disorimen).
Lit.: fac periculum in litteris,: miser est homo qui amat ... Scio qui periclum feci,: priusquam periclum faceret,: ex aliis,: alicujus fidei periculum facere,to make trial of, to try,: quā in re tute tui periculum fecisti,: legionum, Auct. B. Afr. 79.—
Transf.
Concr., an attempt in writing, an essay: faciunt imperite, qui in isto periculo non ut a poëtā, sed ut a teste, veritatem exigent (speaking of a poem in honor of Marius),; .—
Risk, hazard, danger, peril (which acompanies an attempt; the common signif. of the word): meo periclo rem gero,: tuo ego istaec dicam illi periculo,: periculum facere,to run a risk,: si ei subito sit allatum periculum discrimenque patriae,: salus sociorum summum in periculum ac discrimen vocatur,: discriminum et periculorum comites,: obire pericula ac labores,: periculum adire capitis,to run the risk of one's life,: in periculo animarum suarum,: subire pro amico,: suscipere,to take upon one's self,: ingredi,: conflare alicui,to cause, occasion,: intendere in aliquem,: intendere alicui,: mortis alicui inicere,: facessere innocenti,: facere alicui,; cf.: ego nihil facio tibi periculi,: creare alicui,: comparare alicui,: moliri optimis civibus,: amici depellere,: subterfugere,: adducta est res in maximum periculum et extremum paene discrimen,: se in periculum capitis atque in vitae discrimen inferre,: arcessere aliquem in summum capitis periculum,: includere in periculum,: in periculum se committere,to get into danger,: eripere ex periculo,: extrahere ex periculo,to release from danger,: rem publicam a periculo prohibere,: liberare periculis,: res in periculo vertitur,the affair becomes perilous,: esse in periculo,: in periculo versari,: a securi negat ei periculum esse,that danger threatens him,: periculum est, ne,there is danger that,; so : periculo meo, tuo, suo, at my, your, his risk: meo periculo,: crede audacter meo periculo,: meo periculo rem gero,; : des ei nummos fide et periculo meo,: navem sumptu periculoque suo armatam mittere,; : rem periculi sui facere,to do a thing at one's own risk,: bono periculo, safely, without danger (post-class.), .—
In partic.
A trial, action, suit at law (class.): meus labor in privatorum periculis caste integreque versatus,: aliquem in periculis defendere,.—
A writ of judgment, a sentence: unum ab iis petivit, ut in periculo suo inscriberent, etc.,: pericula magistratuum,.—
A sickness, attack of sickness (post-Aug.): in acutis vero periculis nullis dandum est vinum,.—
Ruin, destruction (postclass.): tremefactae nutant usque ad periculum civitates,.

senses: in the same manner, as, just as, quite as, equally
la:adv:perinde.html:
pĕr-inde, adv., a particle of comparison.
in the same manner, just as, quite as, equally; in like manner, just so (class.; cf. proinde, with which it is frequently confounded

in MSS. and edd.).

In gen.: vivendi artem tantam tamque operosam et perinde fructuosam relinquere,: si perinde cetera processissent,: non Pyrrhum, aut Antiochum populo Romano perinde metuendos fuisse,: utilissimum munus, sed non perinde populare,: Mithridates corpore ingenti, perinde armatus, in a corresponding manner, accordingly, Sall. ap. : perinde laudaret castigaretque,; ; .—
In partic., with the conjunctions atque (ac), ut, ac si, quasi, prout, quam, etc. (so most freq.)
With atque (ac), just as, etc.: non perinde atque ego putaram,not exactly as I had expected,: Africam ei perinde ac debellatum in Italiā foret provinciam destinabat,; ; : perinde ac satisfacere et fraudata restituere vellent, just as if, etc., .—
With ut, utcumque, just as, ; : perinde sunt ut aguntur,; cf.: nec perinde ut maluisset plebes, etc.,: perinde ut afficeretur,just as, according as,: perinde utcumque temperatus sit aër, ita, etc.,in whatever way,.—
With ac si, just as if, : quod ego perinde tuebar ac si usus essem,; : perinde aestimans, ac si usus esset,.—
With quasi, just as if, as if, etc.: perinde valebit, quasi armatissimi fuerint,: haec perinde loquor, quasi debueris aut potueris, etc., (but B. and K. read proinde ... quasi, ; ).—(ε) With prout, just according as, —(ξ) With tamquam, just as much as if, just the same as if, .—(η) With et or que, equally with, the same as (Tacitean): perinde odium pravis et honestis,: perinde divina humanaque obtegens,; .—(θ) With ut, so that, to the extent that: habes munus a patre meā quidem sententiā magnum, sed perinde erit ut acceperis,: Julianus nimius religionis Christianae insectator, perinde tamen, ut cruore abstineret,.—(ι) With quam, so much as: nullā tamen re perinde motus est, quam responso mathematici,.—(κ) With quam si, the same as if (postAug.): jusjurandum perinde aestimandum, quam si Jovem fefellisset,.— (λ) Perinde tamquam si, .—(μ) Haud perinde—quam, not as well ... as (post-Aug.), .—
With ellipsis of the second member of the comparison: possessione et usu haud perinde afficiuntur (sc. ac facile expectares),i. e. not so much as one would expect, not very much,; cf.: aurum et argentum non perinde ac reliqui mortales adpetunt,: coxendice et femore et crure sinistro non perinde valebat (sc. ac dextro),: quare adventus ejus non perinde gratus fuit,; ; ; : Romanis haud perinde celebris,

la:adj:peritus.html:
pĕrītus, a, um, adj.
prop. Part. of perior (in ex-perior); root par-, per-; Gr. περάω; v. periculum
,
experienced, practised, practically acquainted, skilled, skilful, expert (cf.: gnarus, consultus).
Lit.
Absol.: nil iam mihi novi Offerri pote, quin sim peritus,: doctos homines vel usu peritos,: docti a peritis,: ab hominibus callidis ac peritis animadversa,: decede peritis,: me peritus discet Iber,: homo peritissimus,: hominem peritissimum in eis ipsis rebus, superare, quas, etc.,: peritissimi duces,; . —
With gen.: multarum rerum peritus,: antiquitatis nostrae et scriptorum veterum litterate peritus,: earum regionum,: caelestium prodigiorum,: peritiores rei militaris,: bellorum omnium peritissimus,: peritissimi caeli ac siderum vates,: juris,: vir movendarum lacrimarum peritissimus,: definiendi,.—
With abl.: jure peritus, Lucil. ap. P.: jure peritissimus,: quis jure peritior?: peritus bello,: peritus disciplinā militari,: arte fabricā peritus,.—
With ad: ad usum et disciplinam peritus,: et ad respondendum et ad cavendum peritus,: ad prospicienda cavendaque pericula,.—(ε) With in and abl.: sive in amore rudis, sive peritus erit, (3, 32), 82.—(ζ) With de: de agriculturā peritissimus,.—(η) With acc. (poet.): arma virumque peritus,.—(θ) With inf. or object-clause (poet. and in post-Aug. prose): soli cantare periti Arcades,: peritus obsequi,: urentes oculos inhibere perita,: rex peritus, fortius adversus Romanos aurum esse quam ferrum,.—Hence, subst.: pĕrītissĭ-mus, i, m., a man of extraordinary skill: cum discendi causā duobus peritissimis operam dedisset, etc.,.—
Transf., of abstract things, skilfully constructed, clever: peritae fabulae,.—Hence, adv.: pĕrītē, in an experienced manner, skilfully, expertly, cleverly: quod institutum perite a Numa,: perite et ornate dicere,; : callide et perite versari in aliquā re,: distributa perite,.— Comp.: peritius fit aliquid ab aliquo,.—Sup.: aliquid peritissime et callidissime venditare,: disputare,: suavissime et peritissime legere,.

la:verb:periclitor.html:
pĕrīclĭtor, ātus, 1 (periclitatus, in
pass. signif.; v.infrafin.), v. dep. a. and n.
periculum
.
Act.
In gen., to try, prove, test any thing, to make a trial of, put to the test (class.; syn.: experior, tento): periclitatus animum sum tuum, quid faceres,: an periclitamini Quid animi habeam,: belli fortunam tentare ac periclitari,: omnia,: fidem alicujus. : in periclitandis experiundisque pueris,: periclitandae vires ingenii,: exerceri in rebus cominus noscendis periclitandisque,.—
In partic., to put in peril, to endanger, risk, jeopard (rare but class.): non est saepius in uno homine salus summa periclitanda rei publicae, Cic.

.—

Neutr.
To try, attempt, make an attempt (class.): periclitari volui, si, etc., Planc. ap. : cotidie quid nostri auderent, periclitabatur,; .—
Pregn., to venture, to be bold or enterprising (post-Aug.): proeliis et periclitando tuti sunt,.—
To be in danger or peril, to incur or be exposed to danger, to be endangered or imperilled (class.): ut potius Gallorum vita quam legionariorum periclitaretur,: ne de summā imperii populus Romanus periclitetur, Aug. ap. .—
With abl.: famā ingenii,: capite,to have one's head in danger, be in danger of losing one's head,: veneno,: paralysi,: causā,to be on trial,.—
With gen. (postclass.): capitis,to be in peril of one's life,.—
With inf. (postAug.): periclitabatur totam paene tragoediam evertere,: rumpi,; .—With ab and abl.: ab obtrectatore,, Serm. 14, 29.—With pro: pro veritate,, Serm. 14, 29.—With propter: propter te cotidie,, Serm. 14, 29: propter peccatum,.—With ex: periclitantes ex canis rabiosi morsu,.—
Trop.: ut verba non periclitentur, that the words may run no danger (of losing the cause), .—Hence, pĕrīclĭtātus, a, um, part. perf.; in pass. signif., tried, tested: periclitatis moribus amicorum,.
